prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1452; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured was changing lanes. The claimant reports a back strain and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will route through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Photographs taken at the scene confirm several details of the reported impact, although no independent witnesses have come forward to describe the collision.

Entry 3: Police report and the statements of other parties confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the crash. The damage pattern on the vehicle matches the impact described by all involved.

Entry 4: No prior damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. The driver is a member of the policyholder's household and is covered as such.

Entry 5: The claimant's medical records show a treatment course typical for this type of injury and force, with care tapering off as the patient improved. No earlier injury to the same body area is on record.

Entry 6: In a follow-up interview, the claimant added a few minor details to the account. The core description of the event remained consistent with the initial report.

Entry 7: Based on the vehicle damage, the photographs, the medical course, and the absence of any prior injury or damage, the reported injury appears well matched to the kind and force of the crash. The file is being reviewed for settlement evaluation with counsel.
